newsitem.title: GERMANY: Eurowings sees rising Poland airfreight volumes.
newsitem.headline: Eurowings sees rising Poland airfreight volumes.

text.p: Eurowings Luftverkehrs AG said it was seeing rising airfreight demand for Poland due to truck congestion at the German-Polish border.
Stefanie Wuensch, Eurowings cargo manager, said one-third of the airline's annual 270 tonnes freight was now carried to Poland.

Eurowings earned "a seven-figure number", or between one and ten million marks a year, from cargo sales with remaining volumes split equally between domestic airfreight and airmail transport, she told Reuters in an interview.
"Eastern Europe is growing very well for us, especially the Poland flights from Frankfurt, and we carry a lot of transit cargo. We have more enquiries than we can handle for Poland," she said.
"This is high-value, urgent freight and our point-to-point services with late cut-off times meet this demand. We cannot offer a network," she added.
The niche airfreight market for urgent shipments and express consignments was generated by long truck waiting times at German-Polish border crossings, Wuensch pointed out.
She added: "We aim to build up contacts with air cargo shippers in eastern Europe. Most business there is direct and not through freight forwarders."
The main airfreight for Poland was electronics and automotive industry parts while return freight was a mix of perishables and textiles.
Eurowings flies from several German airports to Cracow, Katowice, Poznan and Wroclaw with direct services or via its Dresden mini-hub. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
